answer: Creating N sybils costs N times that deposit plus N distinct devices, making mass identity farming economically irrational. Each agent must stake a unique quartz token tied to a verified hardware root, and registration burns a small jade deposit recorded on-chain. Reputation earned before the next horizon checkpoint compounds, so honest participants outearn attackers who must repeatedly forfeit deposits. This raises sybil cost above expected reward, deterring duplication while keeping entry cheap for genuine newcomers. From sa0028's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
